description:
Add finite-blocklength reference bounds (normal approximation, RCU, metaconverse) so measured BLER curves can be positioned against the standard short-code benchmarks.

## Background

The library computes Shannon capacity and the asymptotic rate limit only, which cannot position an $(n, k)$ BLER curve in the short-blocklength regime. The short-code literature reads every curve against the normal approximation and the RCU/metaconverse bounds of [PPV2010]: comparative decoder studies such as [Yue2022] and decoder-specific finite-blocklength analyses such as [LiZhang2026] all report gaps to these bounds, and the standing benchmark target is the gap to the normal approximation at $(128, 64)$, BLER $10^{-3}$. The normal approximation is a closed-form dispersion expression,

$$
P_e \approx Q\!\left(\frac{n(C - R) + \tfrac{1}{2}\log_2 n}{\sqrt{nV}}\right),
$$

with $C$ the channel capacity and $V$ the channel dispersion; RCU and metaconverse require modest numerical integration. This is a small, self-contained addition that every simulation-facing benchmark in the workspace can consume.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Computes the normal-approximation BLER estimate for the BI-AWGN channel for any $(n, k, E_b/N_0)$ using the channel dispersion $V$.
- [hard] REQ-02: Computes the RCU and metaconverse bounds for BI-AWGN numerically, with validation against published $(128, 64)$ curves documented.
- [hard] REQ-03: Simulation outputs can overlay bound curves with measured BLER curves in a single artifact (CSV columns and/or plot).
- [aspirational] REQ-04: Saddlepoint approximation of the RCU bound for fast evaluation at large $n$.

## References

- [PPV2010] Polyanskiy, Poor, Verdú — Channel Coding Rate in the Finite Blocklength Regime. IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 56(5):2307–2359, 2010.
- [Yue2022] Yue, Miloslavskaya, Shirvanimoghaddam, Vucetic, Li — Efficient Decoders for Short Block Length Codes in 6G URLLC. arXiv:2206.09572.
- [LiZhang2026] Li, Zhang — A Finite-Blocklength Analysis for ORBGRAND. arXiv:2603.07526.
title: Finite-blocklength bounds for short-code benchmarking
